title: Pupils grow a prize-winning garden
text:
By Ayu, Class 4A reporter

Pupils at Cempaka Primary School won first prize in the Green Schools Competition last Friday for their vegetable garden.

The garden began last year as a muddy corner behind the school canteen. Class 4A cleared away the weeds, built six raised beds from old wooden boxes, and planted spinach, chillies, tomatoes and long beans. Every morning before lessons, the pupils water the plants with rainwater that they collect in two large barrels.

The judges visited the school on 12 September. They were impressed that the pupils make compost from fruit peel and leaves. “This garden shows what young people can do,” said Mr Hendra, one of the judges. “It is a wonderful example for other schools.”

The vegetables are now used in the school canteen twice a week. Last month, the cooks made spinach soup for 150 pupils with leaves from the garden.

The head teacher, Mrs Wulan, said she was very proud. “The children worked so hard, even in the heavy rain,” she said.

Daniel, who is nine, said his favourite job is checking the tomatoes. “I think our tomatoes taste better than any tomatoes from the shop,” he said.

The class plans to spend the prize money of Rp2.000.000 on fruit trees. They hope to plant mangoes and guavas next term.
